summary: SSE stream epilogue dropped after ingress multi-header sanitization; final paragraphs missing
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long-form streamed responses (SSE) from the hosted API consistently drop the final epilogue — typically the closing paragraph and 'source' metadata — when their client performs a short socket swap (mobile network change) behind our edge.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer opens SSE streaming chat to redwood-curated-7b in prod/us-west with X-Stream-Meta header set as two identical headers (client library adds duplicate header).
2) After ~18s of tokens, client triggers an IP/mobility handoff (WiFi -> cellular) causing a short TCP close/rebind and upstream proxy swap.
3) Client reconnects and requests resume; the session returns prior tokens but the final epilogue and trailing metadata never arrive (stream ends mid-sentence).
4) Repeatable in ~4/10 attempts when duplicate X-Stream-Meta headers present; not reproducible when header is a single consolidated value.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:03:22Z proxy-ingress[edge-03] INFO: incoming SSE start session_id=sn-9f2a X-Stream-Meta=[a,b]
2026-03-10T14:03:40Z serving-runtime[worker-12] WARN: client-socket-flip session=sn-9f2a reconnect detected, resume-request=true
2026-03-10T14:03:41Z proxy-ingress[edge-03] DEBUG: sanitized headers for session sn-9f2a; X-Stream-Meta consolidated="a"
2026-03-10T14:03:41Z serving-runtime[worker-12] ERROR: sse-stream-halfclose session=sn-9f2a tail-buffer-not-flushed; bytes-dropped=512
comments: Customer (Sara @ NoteSpring): We're seeing the assistant cut off mid-paragraph after our users switch networks. It looks like the session resumes but the final section (citation block + closing paragraph) is missing ~40% of the time.
Support (Maya): Thanks — confirmed we can see traces for the sample request you provided. I've escalated to SRE for deeper ingestion/proxy checks and requested pcap and tcpdump from the customer.

SRE (Oliver): Observed edge sanitization logs where multi-valued X-Stream-Meta became single-valued during header normalization. Need packet captures and proxy config to validate whether the final event flush path was suppressed by header state change.
Customer: Attached pcap + curl reproducible steps. We can toggle the client to send a single header as a workaround for now.
Support: Temporary workaround noted; SRE to test hotfix in staging and confirm.
investigation_notes: 1) Telemetry: grafana link shows increased stream-halfclose count for NoteSpring sessions around 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/stream-health?var-customer=NoteSpring).

2) Hypothesis: Edge proxy header sanitizer collapses multi-header X-Stream-Meta values to the first value, which causes the serving runtime to treat the resumed connection as lacking the 'finalize' marker. The runtime then half-closes without flushing trailing buffer to client.
3) Evidence: proxy-ingress debug line 'X-Stream-Meta consolidated="a"' present in failure cases; tcpdump shows original request carried two identical X-Stream-Meta headers before ingress rewrite.
4) Related behavior: Not seen when client sends a single header or when using websocket fallback — implies issue is tied to header parsing path in ingress -> sse adapter.
5) Repro rate: ~40% on NoteSpring reproduction; higher when handoff occurs within 10–30s of stream close.
resolution: Workaround: Instructed NoteSpring to consolidate their client SDK to send a single X-Stream-Meta header (server will accept comma-separated values). Implemented customer-side change and verified missing epilogue no longer reproduces in their test harness. Fix: Rollout PR to ingress-proxy that preserves multiple X-Stream-Meta values (avoids collapsing to first value) merged to staging (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/compare/fix-multiheader-sanitize). Production rollout plan: canary 10% edge nodes 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, monitor sse-halfclose metric for 2 hours, then full rollout. Follow-ups: add unit tests for header normalization, add metric alert for 'sse-tail-drop' and update runbook to include header-multi value check.
